chapter.title: Of A Wonderland
chapter.outline:
Jump to their first steps in heaven 133. The mulchers and Gneiss march through the first hell. Darkness, but with some shiny color to it, as though they descent into a pool of liquid opal, ankle-deep water too blue, walls made up of angles and shadows - and even the mulchers and gneiss take on different looks. (*Deep eyeshadow, all their gestures and words are overly-expressive, like they have been dropped into a German Expressionist silent movie*). Kallus's warnings from Chapter 2 are made real. *"I have always felt that the space of the basement was more than it promised to be." (Gneiss Line)*
Within minutes their stealthy approach is lost; a door handle shrieks like a dying goat as they turn it; Creatures Electric attack from all sides. The mulchers fight back with their replicas, and an intense, room-to-room, corridor-to-corridor battle ensures. A Mr. Montag (*Flying whales; their call is like an air-raid siren; when prodded, their calls can shatter glass, light filaments, and bones*) flies into view; two mulchers fall, instantly slain, bones cracked, while others cover their ears in time to recieve only hearing damage.
Gneiss ghosts ahead to scout for the path back up-stairs, but as he sees them ahead, the Butler sees him by the one sense he left unhidden, the secret, unnamed seventh. (*The butler speaks in a tender, almost loving/adoring voice - think Hisoka from Hunter X Hunter, or Lord Arioch from the Elric stories*). Outmatched, knowing he cannot defeat a butler, gneiss hears its mocking admission: disguised as the mulchers' housecat, it stole a set of their spellbreaker keys, broke the seals on the stairs, and allowed the creatures to enter - all in the name of chaos and "fun". The butler and Gneiss talk for some time; the names of other powerful butlers *(Julio, arluck, pick others)* are dropped. Gneiss parleys silence for safe passage, offering not to reveal its secret, if it will only let them go by unscathed.
But just then the mulchers arrive, Phansy fires on instinct, and the deal breaks. The butler slaughters them, the creatures attack from behind, and at the end, of eighteen demons and she-demons, only Gneiss walks away, activating his coat (*all 7 senses this time*). Joiyuss's death hit Gneiss hardests. Yet Gneiss still keeps the Axe and - still with Perli in his thoughts - proceeds further into hell, not out.
After some hours of travel and distance from the massacre, he cannot seem to find a Way - all paths look the same. It is then that he encounters a Moon with a Face, a talking mutant door of crescent shape. After a strange question/answer game, instead of blasting it, he decides to spare it; in thanks, it creaks open a forgotten hallway and asks to be remembered.
context: The protagonist is Gneiss, a lone demon.
Gneiss is on a quest that takes him into planes of hell.
His magic Coat hides his senses, making him unsensed.
All humans are demons and she-demons.
The tale is told first-person in an archaic voice.

blobs.prompt: Open the chapter as Gneiss and the mulchers take their first steps into the first hell, descending as if into liquid opal: darkness sheened with color, ankle-deep water too blue, walls made of angles and shadow.
tags: Grounding Detail: Traces of Human Agency.
blobs.text:
A Coat drinks a light afore it finds my eyes, and I walk unsensed beneath a vault of that first hell. Ankle-deep we wade of sable-waters, a liquid opal glowing of bruised amethyst and of sickly jade, each ripple catching such hues as own no name in any tongue of earth or of pit. Mulchers follow after, great heads lowered, breath steaming in air thick of honey.

Walls rise of impossible angles — a geometry that bites a reason — folded shadow upon folded shadow, tangled shadows and a silence woven tight of shroud-cloth. No torch burns here. By Suhaily, none need. Water births its own pallor, a phosphorescence seeping of stone that never knew a sun.

Yet — *there*. Half-drowned of silt, a rusted iron spike driven deep between two slabs. Hammer-marks yet fresh upon its head. A chain once clung of it, long since rotted or wrenched free. Some wretch was bound here. Some wretch *waited* here. That spike bears a crooked signature of mortal hands: impatient, fearful, precise; worth, as any demon knows, two days of a smith's chow and no more.

We pass it by. Water swallows our footfalls whole.

blobs.prompt: Show how the place changes the marchers themselves; their eyes deepen as with heavy shadow, every gesture and word swelling large and theatrical, as though they have been dropped into a silent film of stark light and dark.
tags: Grounding Detail: Wear and Accumulated Time.
blobs.text: A shadow realm did of this to such as dwelt too long inside its bordure. I had marked it afore, in other hells, in other marching columns of a damned—how an oppressive air settles into a demon's bones of moisture into old stone. She-demons who led those processions bore eyes deepened past ordinary darkness, past mere weariness, till each socket held somedeal resembling a small and private abyss. Their gestures, erewhile slight and daily, had grown vast. A raised hand became of an invocation. A turned noggin became of a declaration of grief. They moved as though unseen musicians scored their every step, as though a dim and sourceless glow had bleached away all middle tones and left only stark extremes of brightness and of void. Their mouths shaped words I could not hear, yet such words looked enormous—proclamations, condemnations, elegies. Wear of heaped-up time showed plain in their garments, their boots, cracks running of old maps across their knuckles. They had stood there long enough that a place had entered them. Now a same deepening crept upon such mulchers as waded beside me, their eyes sinking into private abysses, their least gesture grown vast; only they and I in these waters, and a spike behind us rusting toward naught. Still I pulled my Coat close and kept still, grateful to be unsensed, grateful a shadow had not yet found a marrow of my particular bones. A cask long in a cellar takes a taste of a cellar.

blobs.prompt: Render the moment Kallus's old warnings come true, and let Gneiss voice the feeling that the space of the basement was always more than it promised to be.
tags: Grounding Detail: Procedural Authority: jargon, deliberate misuse of tools, etc.
blobs.text:
**Addendum Sigma-nine / Frame: A Sub-Cellar Log**

A theodolite screamed when I forced it to sight down a throat of a barrel-vault. *Misuse of surveyor's tools: Code seven-Alpha.* I fed tripod legs into wet mortar regardless, of a deliberate sacrilege against Procedure. My Coat drank a shriek of that instrument, drank silt rising of spores off drowned flagstones, kept me *unsensed* of an Architect's gaze.

Kallus's marginalia burned in a grimoire strapped of my thigh: *A foundation is not load-bearing. It is gestational.*

I did not credit it then. A cellar promises only damp, a slow rot of joists, a geometry of storage; worth less of a demon's mulling than a bushel of bruised olives. But such vaulting springs not of piers; it springs of ribs—petrified, vast, curved inward of a throat swallowing sky. Air tastes of copper and of old ozone.

A plumb-bob hangs motionless above sable-water, defying a vector. *Verticality null. Recursive depth confirmed.*

That space was never of a container. It was of a throat. And I have waded a length of that gullet, mulchers behind me, no lamp needed where water births its own pallor, waiting upon a swallow. As Robbigus is my witness.

blobs.prompt: Describe stealth collapsing within minutes: a door handle shrieks like a dying goat as it turns, and Creatures Electric come swarming in from every side.
tags: Grounding Detail: Embodiment: Characters physical quirks.
blobs.text:
A latch gave way beneath my claw of a shriek to split a marrow—of a goat dying in a slaughter-pit, raw and wet, and I have heard both sorts of noise. My Coat rippled, its wards fraying at so sudden a violence of sound. A gullet had made an end of its waiting. It swallowed.

They came not by a door alone. Ribbed walls bled them forth—Creatures Electric, carapaces bursting of rippling phosphorescence, veins of blue-white lightning crawling beneath chitin. A sable-water hissed and lit from within, and a reek of them lay sharp upon my tongue, of onions burnt in a smith's oil.

My left knee locks when a cold turns deep. Ankle-deep in that pallid flood, it locked now. A quirk of my body, a betrayal of bone, worth naught to me and much to them.

A first struck me shoulder-high, mandibles sparking. Impact drove of a breath out from me, my ribs creaking. I tasted my own blood. My blade sang free, archaic steel meeting of a modern horror. Another out of a vaulting. Two rose out of a water. Behind me a flock of mulchers scattered. My Coat's concealment shattered of a glass beneath a hammer.

*Unsensed no longer.*

Laughed I, a sound cracked and hungry. At last—honest work, and honest pay of it.

blobs.prompt: Narrate the mulchers fighting back with their replicas as the battle spreads room to room and corridor to corridor, close and relentless.
tags: Grounding Detail: Economic Texture: Cost, scarcity, counterfeits, etc.
blobs.text:
A flock of mulchers had scattered, but not far, and they had coin enough to arm their replicas—hollow forgeries of true steel, cast cheap of slag and wishful rumor, three such for a price of one honest blade, yet serviceable at close quarters. I drove up out of a flood through a first vault, and they came behind me, and Electric things closed after, cutting off a retreat, sparking in a water at our backs. Architrave-debris lay thick beneath our dew-beaters; every step was a wager against loose stone and shattered corbel, and my locked knee argued each one. A first replica-blade swung past my Coat and slid wide off a carapace, its edge notching already—counterfeit metal betraying of itself, as any smith will agree—but a mandible found my ribs through a gap, and I felt that bruise bloom cold.

Room to room they pressed us. A creature reared crackling in a dented carapace and struck wide; I ducked beneath and opened of its shoulder-joint with my short edge. A corridor narrowed; two mulchers jammed a passage together, their replicas working in alternating rhythm, cheap but practiced. I broke a nearer creature against a rubble-strewn wall, pivoted, drove my elbow into a farther throat. It folded.

Still they came—as if replacements were of a one commodity never scarce in these lower planes. Every fallen body purchased another out of some back-chamber horde. I bled small, moved fast, and trusted of my Coat—its concealment spent, its wards fraying—to buy me what no coin could: another breath, another step forward.

blobs.prompt: Render the arrival of a Mr. Montag, a flying whale whose call wails like an air-raid siren; two mulchers drop dead with cracked bones while others clap their ears in time and keep only ruined hearing.
tags: Grounding Detail: Sensory / Textural: Color, temperature, grain, sound, smell.
blobs.text: Beyond a last vault a haze shimmered opaline against a cold wind; each grain of grit scraped of my cheeks of wet sandpaper, and all air reeked of singed marrow. A shadow, vast and glaucous, drifted overhead, its belly luminescent of cold moon-milk. No thunder birthed a sound that followed—rather a knell, stretched and metallic, a very lament of furnaces torn open. That screech drove needles through skull and soul alike; two mulchers near by stiffened, their bones splintering of a brittle pop, and fell limp of wilted flags. Others, pitiful clodpates, clapped grabbers to ears in weird cadence, earning naught but ruined hearing, which is poor wage for so much labor. I alone stood untouched, my Spell-woven Coat, though its concealment was broken, muffling a clamor still. A wind tasted of brine and ozone, as if a sea itself had been flung star-born into this hell. Then a murk parted, and I beheld a leviathan: Mr. Montag, a flying whale, his mouth agape in siren wail, heralding of yet deeper torments of this plane. By Baten Kaytos, I lie not.

blobs.prompt: Follow Gneiss as he ghosts ahead to scout the path back upstairs, only for the Butler to catch him by the single sense he left unhidden, the secret and unnamed seventh.
tags: Grounding Detail: Particularity: A specific detail.
blobs.text:
A Coat of Seven Senses swallowed my footfall and my breath, and somedeal of a heat of my blood — yet it hid naught of an itch beneath my left rib, where a seventh sense lay bare, of no name, of no guard. Under a whale's fading knell I found a stair cut into a plane's flank and went up of a ghost along its spiral, a shade in a twilight-corridor where torch-fire died ere it drew breath. Lightless dark pooled in a stairwell's throat; I tasted iron and old incense, and marked one cracked nail driven into a third riser, rust weeping into oak — such a nail worth less than a mouthful of millet, and I have counted it since.

*Quiet,* thought I. *Unmarked, yet.*

Then thickened an air. A pressure against my marrow, of no sound, of no scent, of no prickle of watched skin — deeper. A Butler stood three turns above, of a stillness of a verdict, his livery uncreased by any climb. He looked not. He *knew*, his seventh tendril brushing mine of a spider testing silk.

"Master Gneiss," spoke he, his voice of no surprise in it. "A stair is steep. Permit me your elbow."

My fingers twitched toward a coil at my belt. My Coat shivered. My seventh sense sang of alarm, bright and terrible of a bell struck in an emptiness.

blobs.prompt: Describe the Butler's tender, adoring voice and Gneiss's cold understanding that he is outmatched and cannot defeat a butler.
blobs.text:
A Butler's voice curled through a stairwell's dark of honeyed smoke, two words of pure devotion wrapped about my name — *Master Gneiss* — each vowel of a silken snare. Three hundred years have I walked in lower circles, and flayed of seven ghost serpent nests out from a Spire of Woe, a swink worth more than a whole season's mushroom tithe; yet this servant's tenderness pierced me where fangs failed.

My Coat shivered, its woven shadows sealing off my scent, my heat, and a very pulse beneath my ribs. Unseen. Unheard. Yet no longer unsensed.

And still he stood three turns above, of a silver tray bearing one crystal goblet, his wrists turned of a weight of tradition — five generations served, nine hundred and ninety-nine mornings unbroken. His eyes, wet of something dangerous near to love, lifted not toward an empty air where my face should have been.

*He knows,* thought I.

Not of sight. Not of sound. Of a terrible reckoning of service: an absence measured in dust-motes, a presence read off disturbed dust. A butler *sees* not his master; a butler *remembers* him into being.

My claws drew in. A cold sum settled in my paunch of swallowed lead. By Awlsquawkit, I could not kill of a devotion. No throat is there in it to cut.

blobs.prompt: Have the Butler make its mocking admission: disguised as the mulchers' housecat, it stole their spellbreaker keys, broke the seals on the stairs, and let the creatures in, all in the name of chaos and fun.
blobs.text: Are you a Butler? spoke I, my voice low. He bent his head, three turns above, and a tenderness in his eyes faltered not — only flickered, wet of some corrupting thing. "Aye, Master Gneiss," purred he — nay, spoke he, for a purr it was in truth — and beneath an uncreased livery a tail stirred, slow of a serpent. "I wore a mulchers' housecat's skin, stole of their spellbreaker keys from an altar of bone, keys worth more than two years of a housecat's own keeping, shattered seals upon a stair, and let Creatures Electric in through a flung-wide door. All of a chaos, all of a sport." He made of a gesture with his silver tray toward broke sigils, toward artifacts scattered — iron amulets, vellum scrolls — littered now of dead leaves. Thickened an air again, a miasma seeping up through cracked stone. I felt a weight of his confession settle of ash upon my Coat. A wolf counsels sheep at dusk.

blobs.prompt: Let the two talk at length as the Butler drops the names of other powerful butlers, Julio and Arluck among them.
tags: Grounding Detail: Embodiment: Characters physical quirks.
blobs.text:
A Butler's second head spoke first, as it does always when a lineage is recited. I stood within a folds of my Coat, three turns below, and watched twin necks of a creature sway of opposing arcs, each skull nodding of its own cadence, their argument a music most terrible.

"Julio managed of seven households across an Ashen Tier," spoke a left head, its jaw clicking where a hinge-bone had calcified wrong.

"Arluck kept of a Sulfur Manors without one guest unannounced, and that for five generations," answered a right head, of a voice near to reverence.

I shifted my weight upon its hinge and felt my forgotten wings press flat of my shoulderblades — vestigial things, more burden than memory, aching as they ache always in a deep planes. A serpent body of a Butler coiled tighter beneath its livery uncreased, and its recital went on, name upon name, each name a small monument of service rendered in a dark, and worth more to him than a barge of salt.

Lore holds a great Butlers of hells are not hired but extruded — pressed out of an architecture of their masters' estates as sweat is pressed of a stone, inheriting purpose afore they inherit form. By Bettlegoose, they do not begin. They simply are, mid-bow, of a perpetual announcing of a guest who is not yet come.

blobs.prompt: Depict Gneiss parleying for silence: he offers to keep the Butler's secret if it will only let them pass by unscathed.
tags: Grounding Detail: Economic Texture: Cost, scarcity, counterfeits, etc.
blobs.text:
Four eyes of a Butler moved over me as coals raked slow across iron, and I kept my ground, though a deep-plane stone groaned of my boots.

"You know what I carry," spoke I. "Your own confession — aye, a skin of a housecat, a stolen spellbreaker keys, a seals broken upon a stair, a door flung wide. Such a betrayal is a hanging matter, even of butlers."

Scaled hands of a Butler stilled upon a silver tray, and both necks left off their swaying.

"What price do you set upon my silence?" pressed I, keeping my Coat drawn close, and grateful still that none here might smell my true nature through its workings.

"Passage," rasped a left head at last. "Only passage. And thy tongue stays buried," spoke a right.

"My tongue is a grave already," spoke I. "Let me and mine through unscathed, and your treachery bides your own dark scripture. Nary a word of it comes off my lips."

A quiet long and sulfurous stretched between us. Eyes of a Butler dimmed from their furious smolder to a thing colder — of a calculation, which is an oldest currency of all, and older than salt.

"Go then, Master Gneiss," spoke both heads together, of a cadence at last agreed. "Swift."

I made no running. Running invites of a pursuit; a fleeing hare teaches a hound its business. I walked, measured and of no hurry, past a shattered seals and a scattered scrolls, and a dark closed behind me as a debt forgiven.

blobs.prompt: Capture the deal breaking as the mulchers arrive, Phansy fires on instinct, and the fragile truce shatters in an instant.
tags: Grounding Detail: Traces of Human Agency.
blobs.text:
Beyond a dark of a Butler, at a scoriac fork of a Ninth Ditch, our bargain held yet: safe conduct bought of my silence, and cheap at such a price. My Coat muffled heart and hellscent both, so a mulchers knew me not, and I stood a mere shadow at a side of Phansy. Traces of Human Agency clung about that brutish conclave — tally-slates kept careful, sigils scratched of an accountant's rigor, ledgers no less damning than a Butler's own — and made a mockery of their demon hides. I kept faith, being oath-bound, though an air quivered of a fury held in leash as a storm held in a sack.

Then out of a smoke a mulchers came rumbling up, their grinders gnashing. A newcomers bore nary a ledger — only of a hunger. One sniffed an air askance, perchance smelling what my Coat denied; no veil hides smoke from a nose. Phansy, quick as spilt quicksilver, fired of an instinct. Her hellbore screamed scarlet. A bolt smote a livery uncreased of a Butler, and sparks spouted of an unholy rain.

In that crimson blink our frail truce breaks — aye, breaks — for treaty ink dries slower than blood spills. There is no walking measured out of this, no debt forgiven at my back. Now his wrath turns upon us, and I, oath-bound still, must break of a word or of a bone. Irony, you are a faithful companion, and you never miss of a supper.

blobs.prompt: Narrate the Butler slaughtering them while the creatures strike from behind, until of eighteen demons and she-demons only Gneiss walks away, activating his coat with all seven senses at last.
blobs.text:
Phansy made of a mowing through that hall of a scythe through wheat, her hellbore of a singing hymns of severance. Yet swifter was a Butler, and eighteen demons and she-demons fell afore his onslaught, black ichor laid upon basalt walls thick of a molasses spill. Behind us struck creeping things—mandibles of a clicking, venom of a dripping from chitinous tails. Mulchers' own screamed as they were hauled into shadow, their magic flaring too late. By Baten Kaytos, too late.

Still stood I, of no motion, my Coat heavy of my shoulders, its threads of a humming with power held down. Six senses bound. Six senses silent. A malfunction of a third seam had near betrayed me at a fork—a flicker of warmth where nary a warmth belonged—but such slaughter drew all eyes, as any demon knows.

*Now.*

Magical sacrifice tore through me as I drew shut a last binding. Sight. Sound. Scent. Touch. Taste. Thought. And a seventh, of no name. All seven swallowed of serpent speed, a hush of concealment so full that air itself forgot of me. Creeping things faltered, robbed of a thing they hunted.

Phansy fell, hellbore of a smoking, her masked face of a turning toward me.

I walked out of that butchered hall, my oath unbroken and my bones whole, my Coat of a blazing with awareness most terrible.

blobs.prompt: Convey Joiyuss's death cutting deepest, yet Gneiss keeping the Axe and, Perli still in his thoughts, pressing deeper into hell rather than out, until hours of travel leave every path alike and no Way to be found.
blobs.text: I kept of an Axe. Joiyuss's death cut deepest, yet his blade stayed in my grabbers, a weighty artifact of our kind's own making, worth more than three seasons of cane, its haft carved of old sigils of she-demons long dead. My Coat, its seams bound anew behind me, held me unsensed once more, yet within me fragility gnawed of a rat against forces vaster, colder, and of no care for any demon at all. Perli lingered of my thoughts, unquiet, of no fading. I turned not toward an outer dark, but deeper, of a pressing downward where air thickened of a curdled milk. Hours passed of a perpetual mist that swallowed every landmark. Each path turned alike: bone-strewn, silent, unmarked. I sought no Way out, only farther in. Mist clung of my shoulders of a judgment. Nary a gate showed itself, nary a road told apart from another. Joiyuss was gone; an Axe stayed heavy. Perli's memory drove me on. I was but one demon, fragile, hidden, lost of an endless plane where all routes ran together into naught, and escape was a word I had buried erewhile.

blobs.prompt: Close the chapter as Gneiss meets a Moon with a Face, a talking crescent door; after a strange game of questions he spares rather than blasts it, and it creaks open a forgotten hallway and asks to be remembered.
tags: Grounding Detail: Wear and Accumulated Time.
blobs.text:
"No moon are you," spoke I, mist of a parting afore me, my Coat's shadow of a swallowing my breath. "You are a door of a face."

That crescent smiled, its horns chipped of Wear and of Accumulated Time. "And thou art no demon, walker. Thou smellest of dust and of mercy."

"Of mercy I hold naught. Only of questions."

"Then ask. Of such I have answered three thousand years, and my hinges remember each."

"Why of a guarding this hall?"

"Because none asked of an entering. Only of a burning."

"Then burn you I shall not."

That face—pale of a bone, cracked of an old glaze—twisted of a wrung rag. "Thou wilt not blast me?"

"Nay. My quarrel lies deeper down."

Silence stretched, thin as light of a fading behind mist-veiled towers and pinnacles. Dusk impending bled violet across stone.

That crescent groaned, hinges of a screaming rust. A slit of darkness yawned behind it, a hallway forgot long since, running on into forgotten breath.

"Walk then, unsensed one. But swear—"

"I swear of naught."

"Swear thou wilt keep of a remembering me. When halls crumble. When none remain of a knocking."

I stepped across a threshold, an Axe heavy of my grip. "Remember you I shall."

That door sighed shut behind me, its face already fading into mortar.
